en: Mount Mayon in Albay is a classic stratovolcano famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
Baguio City receives the highest average annual rainfall in the Philippines due to its high elevation and mountainous terrain.
The rich volcanic soil in Benguet province makes it an ideal environment for growing temperate vegetables like cabbage.
Romblon province is famous for its abundant marble deposits, which are metamorphic rocks formed from limestone.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Philippines is located near the equator, which is why the country experiences nearly equal hours of daylight and darkness year-round.
Ancient Filipino farmers used the Pleiades star cluster, locally called Moroporo, to determine the beginning of the planting season.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes the daily rise and fall of ocean tides along the coast of Batangas.
The Marikina Valley Fault System is an active geological fault that poses a significant earthquake hazard to Metro Manila.
The southwest monsoon, locally known as Habagat, brings heavy rains to the western parts of the Philippines during the summer.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of thousands of cone-shaped karst limestone mounds formed by weathering.
Because the Earth's axis is tilted, the Philippines experiences a dry season and a wet season instead of four distinct seasons.
